grh_0219eb22a446d7a80f63.title: Tomorrow Is Forever
paragraphs: Lieutenant John MacDonald is horribly wounded and reported dead at the end of World War I. Believing his shattered body and face would only destroy the life of his young wife Elizabeth, he lets her think he died and builds a new identity as Austrian chemist Erik Kessler. Elizabeth, pregnant with Johnâ€™s child, eventually marries her kind employer Larry Hamilton and raises her son Drew in a loving home. More than twenty years later Kessler comes to work for Larry and quietly meets the son he never knew, just as another war is beginning. Elizabeth gradually recognizes John beneath the altered face and confronts him with their old memories, but he refuses to reclaim her, insisting that Larry is now her true husband and that the past must remain past. He brings Drew home after the boy tries to leave for Canada to enlist, then tells Elizabeth to let their son follow his conscience. Kessler dies the next morning, leaving Elizabeth to understand that his final act of love was to protect the life she built without him.

grh_025b085c183422568ebd.title: The Assassin
paragraphs: A counter-terror operation in Athens tracks a committee preparing to murder an elderly chief justice and his wife. Surveillance agent Charles Holland and police position cameras, marksmen and observers around the hotel while the hired assassin waits across the street with a machine pistol. The attack still exacts a terrible price: the justice and his wife are killed, a security man and bystanders are wounded, and the gunman escapes hurt. Holland then uses the conspirators' effort to hide the wounded assassin to bring the killer and the committee members together in one hotel room, giving police the chance to take the group at once.

paragraphs: The story follows Lou Gehrig from a powerful Columbia ballplayer into a Yankees rookie, his romance and marriage with Eleanor, and the long run of durability that earns him the name the Iron Man.
